probe.format_note: Single 16:9 film, 736x414 (low resolution, small labels are soft), 30 fps; video stream 2398 frames (79.93 s), container 80.11 s. Audio: AAC HE-AACv2 stereo 44.1 kHz, mean -16.4 dB, peak -1.2 dB; silent below -40 dB only at 8.34-8.68 s and from 79.48 s to the end. Measured on the waveform, not heard: a steady pulse near 117.5 BPM (beat 0.511 s, autocorrelation strength 0.585); level about -15 to -19 dB per 5 s, dropping to -27 dB in the 25-30 s and 60-65 s windows. Whether a voice is present was not determined.

reference_name: تایپوگرافی روی تاریکی با نور آبی و قرمز

mode.why: reference of unknown origin (owner note): borrow its motion language and look only, never its shots one by one, its copy, its product or its interface; a voiceover package defaults to REEL, and L4 may choose UI when the package itself is a software or workflow launch

ignored.why: all English copy (a pitch for an architecture design product) and its claims are third-party text; never reused as text, topic or argument
the product name and its star-like logo mark are the creator's brand; the same applies at 55.2-56.47 s and 75.33-79.93 s; our film carries only our own logo per the brand

the floor-plan editor (walls, rooms, furniture, dimension fields, panels) is the reference's product, here and at 21.17-29.87, 31.33-33.63, 38.97-40.97, 47.4-49.13 and 64.23-68.2 s; never copied as a design; only how an interface is framed, tilted and travelled through is borrowed

the three portraits of people, and the names on the cursor pills, are third-party content; no portrait is reused, traced or imitated; a row of images inside a sentence is used only for owner assets or images the voice-over needs
the landscape images with a reflective monolith, and the architecture images at 70.57-72.33 s, are the reference's content; never reused; our scenes take their subjects from the voice-over
the audio track is third-party; L2 uses our voice-over and L6 builds our sound

method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 (14 sheets, 4x3, all viewed; their frames can lag the nominal time by up to 0.25 s, so cut times come from detection, not from the sheets); scene detect gt(scene,0.3) found only 4 cuts (4.77, 54, 59.03, 75.33 s) because the film is dark, so it was rerun at gt(scene,0.07); 12 dense sheets viewed: 0-1.2 s, 4.6-7.0 s, 9-11 s, 13.2-15.6 s, 15.4-19.4 s, 20.2-22.6 s, 22.8-26.8 s, 39-41.4 s, 41.2-44.8 s, 45-48 s, 54.6-57 s, 70-73 s (fps 6 to 15). Cuts at 4.0, 16.2, 20.3, 23.63, 44.2, 55.2 and 72.8 s were read by eye (about ±0.1 s; 4.0 s about ±0.2 s). silencedetect and volumedetect on the audio; a spectral-flux onset script for tempo and cut alignment over 41 cuts. Audio not heard. Colours read by eye, not sampled.

visual_language: A dark, cinematic software launch film built on kinetic type, about 92% buildable in code by shot time. Medium: pure type, a modern dark interface, and out-of-focus close-ups of a glossy abstract 3D form used as the world's only scenery. Typography is the backbone: nearly every second shot is words alone, centred on the frame in one geometric sans (regular weight, tight tracking), mostly one line, with extreme scale contrast from a small line (cap height about 6%) to a word overflowing the frame (about 45%). The main entrance is a slam: the first word starts huge, letter-spaced and motion-blurred, shrinks to rest in about 0.3 s (fast ease-out) and keeps a slow scale-down, while following words reveal left to right through a soft blur (0.3-0.5 s) with gaps that close as the line settles. Variations carry the meaning: a selection box growing with a typed word, a swapping last word carried by a blue light streak, a digital slice glitch, a large caret typing, an image or glossy icon sitting inside the sentence and growing to replace it. One word or word group in each line has a colour gradient as the only emphasis. Rhythm: 50 shots in 79.9 s, about 1.6 s on average (from 0.33 to about 4.6 s), alternating fast between a type shot and a demonstration; cuts follow the phrases, not the music (22% of 41 cuts fall within 50 ms of the 0.511 s pulse, against 20% by chance). Interface shots show one action only (draw, press, type, drag), first as a tight or strongly tilted macro with depth of field, then as a pull-back to the whole window floating in 3D. Palette: pure black, one electric blue world for making things and an orange and sky blue world for people working together; white and metallic grey type. Signature moments: zoom through a pressed button; the sentence that gives up its image to the next shot; the swapping word on a blue streak; the pixel wave with a neon outline; the giant typed word; the logo assembling from scattered pieces at both ends.
look: Dimensionality is mixed: flat type and interface elements placed on real 3D-tilted planes, in front of real 3D glossy forms. Materials: smooth glossy black glass or lacquer with thin curved rim highlights; brushed metal with fine grain on the logo chevron; translucent glossy blue plastic-glass for the icon; dark charcoal interface surfaces with very soft inner shading and rounded corners; metallic grey-white gradients on the type. Light: narrow strip lights reflected along edges, saturated and blown out to white at the core (electric blue, or orange fading to sky blue); everything else falls to pure black; glows on active interface elements and name-tag pills. Depth: the background is always heavily out of focus; tilted macro shots have strong lens blur at top and bottom; the blur clears during pull-backs. Motion blur on type is strong, mostly horizontal. Background: pure black void, no floor, no horizon, with the form cropped by the frame edges.
code_translation: Fully buildable in code apart from image content. Per D55 the background is built as real 3D in three.js, never flattened: one extruded rounded form with MeshPhysicalMaterial (low roughness, clearcoat, black base), narrow RectAreaLights or an emissive strip environment map producing the rim highlights, two light rigs (blue; orange to sky blue), a slow camera drift, depth of field as post blur; brushed metal variant with a roughness and noise map; the 3D icon as a rounded extruded shape with transmission and rim light. Tilted interfaces are HTML or SVG on a CSS 3D plane (or a three.js plane with an HTML texture), with mask-based blur at the top and bottom for depth of field. Word slam: per-word transform scale (about 3 to 1) with an SVG horizontal blur filter clearing over 0.3 s and letter-spacing closing; blur wipe: a moving soft mask plus directional blur, on the whole shaped word in the brand Persian font, right to left (rtl-grammar.md). Blue streak: a horizontal gradient bar and a stretched blurred copy of the word trailing behind it, with additive blending. Slice glitch: canvas or SVG slices offset on the whole word, blue to white. Pixel wave: a canvas grid of blue and white squares driven by a travelling threshold, with a neon stroke-dashoffset outline leading it. Name-tag pills: rounded HTML with a glow and a pointer arrow. Timing from audio.json word times.
continuity: Light as chapter code: the same dark world holds through the film, and only the colour of its light changes with the topic (blue for making, orange and sky blue for working together).
One object, many angles: every type shot sits on another cropped, out-of-focus angle of one glossy form, so hard cuts still feel like one place.
Word to object to scene: an image or icon sitting inside a sentence grows until it replaces the sentence, then lands in its place in the next scene without a cut in its motion.
Zoom through a control: pressing a button accelerates the camera into it, and its interior becomes the next scene.
Detail to whole: a tight or tilted macro pulls back continuously to the full object floating in 3D, depth of field clearing on the way.
Sentence split by proof: a sentence starts in one type shot, a demonstration runs, and the next type shot finishes it.
Pointer characters: small colour-coded name-tag pointers stand for people and carry the action across close-ups, one colour per person.
Selection box on the type: the type itself is treated as an object being edited, so text and interface share one language.
Fixed line, swapped word: one line stays while its last word changes through a streak of light, listing items without a cut.
Pixel wave as making: anything that gets made arrives through a travelling field of squares that resolve to the finished thing.
Vertical hand-over: text accelerates out of the top as the next content rises from below.
Scale ramp by repetition: a repeated word returns larger on each cut.
Bookend: the opening's light and logo move return unchanged at the end.
risks: Reference of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy its product, name, logo, interface design, floor plans, copy, portraits, image content, audio or its shot order one by one.

The reference is 16:9 and the default film is 9:16: its long single lines and wide windows do not fit. L5 must re-compose: stack lines, keep the inline-image idea, frame macros vertically, follow safe-zones.md. Its scale contrast is kept, its literal widths are not.

Persian text: per-letter scatter, letter-by-letter blur wipe, slice glitch by letter and letter-by-letter typing can break joined letters. Run these on whole shaped words or on a correctly shaped text string as rtl-grammar.md allows, placed right to left; the mirror of the left-to-right wipe, slide and caret direction is needed; logo pieces only from the brand's own logo, within brand rules.

Readability: blur, slam and small-line hold times are very short and many words appear for under 1 s. Our voice-over and the minimum sizes and hold times come first (router item 2); keep the entrance motion and lengthen the hold.
Rhythm depends on density: 50 shots in 80 s need enough voice phrases and scenes. On a shorter film keep the alternation of type and demonstration rather than the literal shot count.

Palette: map the blue and orange worlds onto brand colour roles, keep the materials and light behaviour; banned brand colours are never used. Orange is the second chapter colour here; if the brand has no second accent, keep a single light colour and mark chapters by the light's angle or strength. Colours were read by eye, not sampled.

Low source resolution (736x414): small labels and fine detail were soft; move durations are accurate to about ±0.1 s, and cuts read by eye are listed in method. The 7 by-eye cuts were not part of the 41-cut alignment test.

Image-based shots (r1-s13, r1-s14, r1-s38, r1-s47, and the result image in r1-s35) need real image content: use them only with owner assets or images the voice-over needs; never source faces of real people. If there are none, use glossy 3D objects as in r1-s31 instead.
Audio was measured, not heard: tempo and level only, voice presence unknown; the reference's cut rhythm follows phrases, so our cuts follow voice timing from audio.json.
